title: Stall torque measured: 0.32 N*m per motor with an 11.5% dead zone -- the fit's soft motor is refuted, and so is the whole standing recipe
script: robot/sysid_stall.py (lever 58 mm on port A, kitchen scale; operator ran several sessions, last one counts)
question: What is the L motor's real stall torque (GUESS 0.25 since bringup; the joint fit pushed it to 0.10 as one of two load-bearing legs of the first standing sim config)?
headline: Battery-corrected line through 7 stalled duty steps (encoder creep <= 10 deg even at 60%): stall_torque = 0.316 N*m per motor at 7.4 V (0.35 excluding the sticky 15% point), dead zone 11.5% duty -- independently confirming the measured 10% motor friction. The fit's 0.10 is refuted: the real motor is 3x stronger. With run 37 having killed the 4.6 Hz fusion, BOTH legs of the standing plant are now dead -- it was a compensation artifact. The autopsy is productive: the env's motor model applies friction only when moving (kinetic-only), so sim small duties produce torque at zero speed where the real motor produces NOTHING below 11.5%. Scaling stall to 0.10 was the optimizer's way of faking that dead zone. The dead zone is now measured physics and goes into the motor model directly; the refit runs with stall pinned to this measurement and fusion capped at run 37's.
